Unlike [GPU Mesh Voxelization via Axis-Aligned Projection](2561-gpu-mesh-voxelization-via-axis-aligned-projection.md) which explicitly selects the optimal projection axis per triangle to maximize coverage, this method swizzles geometry to align with the XY plane while iterating through bounding boxes to verify 3D overlaps [S3].

The evidence in Source [S3] explicitly describes a method that 'swizzles' geometry by calculating the triangle normal, determining the dominant axis, and permuting vertex coordinates to align the dominant plane with the XY plane ('Swizzle Triangle' section). It further details iterating through bounding boxes ('Bounding Box Calculation') and checking for 3D overlaps by verifying conditions in XY, YZ, and ZX planes ('X-Y Loop', 'Z-Loop', 'Write Voxel'). This matches the description in the claim that the method 'swizzles geometry to align with the XY plane while iterating through bounding boxes to verify 3D overlaps'. The claim contrasts this with another method (GPU Mesh Voxelization via Axis-Aligned Projection) which selects the optimal projection axis per triangle; while the evidence does not describe the other method, the claim is structured as a comparison where the facts attributed to 'this method' (S3) are fully supported by the text.
